title: PhilSCAT 22 (NSIC Rc 818H) Hybrid Rice: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PhilSCAT 22 (NSIC Rc 818H) Rice: Yield and Maturity
metaDescription: PhilSCAT 22 is NSIC Rc 818H, a hybrid rice for irrigated lowland: about 115 days and 9.2 tonnes per hectare on average. See its ratings.
excerpt: NSIC Rc 818H is a hybrid rice variety for irrigated lowland, sold as PhilSCAT 22 and known locally as Mestiso 173. The NSIC approved it in 2026. CLSU and PhilSCAT bred it. It matures in about 115 days and averages 9.2 tonnes per hectare.

heroImage.alt: Ripe palay heads, the harvest a hybrid like NSIC Rc 818H is bred to fill

blocks.text: If you came here looking for PhilSCAT 22, or rice variety 818H, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 9.2 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 184 cavans of 50 kilograms.
**Holds up against:** stem borer, rice blast.
**Watch out for:** green leafhopper, brown planthopper, tungro.
**Cooked rice:** low amylose, so soft and tender.

blocks.caption: From PhilRice's catalogue of released varieties (t/ha means tonnes per hectare)

blocks.text: How much does NSIC Rc 818H yield?

On average it gives 9.2 tonnes per hectare. That is about 184 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits above the average of the 180 irrigated lowland hybrids in PhilRice's list, which is 6.9 tonnes. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 115 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

When you see the first signs, check the guide before you spray, because the right timing saves more than an extra dose. If you are not sure what you see, our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) help you name it from the damage.

blocks.text: Amylose decides how rice cooks. With low amylose, expect rice that is soft. In fact, PhilRice notes that Filipino taste moved from high to intermediate and low amylose rice, because people want it softer.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: Is PhilSCAT 22 the same as NSIC Rc 818H?
items.a: Yes. PhilSCAT 22 is the name it is sold under, and NSIC Rc 818H is its registration with the National Seed Industry Council, where its local name is Mestiso 173. The numbers on this page are PhilRice's for NSIC Rc 818H.

items.q: What is the local name of NSIC Rc 818H?
items.a: It is known as Mestiso 173. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does NSIC Rc 818H take to harvest?
items.a: About 115 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of NSIC Rc 818H?
items.a: PhilRice lists 9.2 tonnes per hectare on average, about 184 cavans of 50 kilograms. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.
Yes. So buy new seed each season, because seed saved from a hybrid crop does not grow true and yields less.

items.q: What should I watch for when I plant it?
items.a: In PhilRice's tests it was weak against green leafhopper, brown planthopper, tungro. So scout from the early weeks and act at the first signs.
